code: Right, Left, Right, Right, Left, Left, Right, Left, Right, Left, Left, Right
effect: Sound test (BOMBERMAN MAX SOUND TEST): music and effect numbers
note: On the title menu (Normal Game / Battle Game / Pitch Area), then A. The menu routine ($01:5F7E in Blue) compares each new press with the 12-byte table $01:5FCD (Red $01:5F87, Hikari $01:54BB, Yami $01:5475, Ain $01:6013); a wrong press starts over. Shown in Mesen in all five versions. GameFAQs lists it for Blue, Red and the Ain Version; Hikari and Yami have the same table.

effect: Own Heat Rock, the unused Charabom (Lv 50)
note: GameShark, cart RAM: $A1F0 is the owned byte of Charabom 28 in the roster table $A110 + 8 x id. No stage or event sets it. The game reads the table in place, so the card shows on Charabom Select at once and stays after a save. Shown in Mesen in all five versions.

effect: Own Oct Kong, the unused Charabom (Lv 50)
note: GameShark, cart RAM: $A1F8, the owned byte of Charabom 29. Shown on Charabom Select in Mesen (all five versions).
GameShark, cart RAM: $A1E0, the owned byte of Charabom 26 (the game's own message is "You have rescued the legendary Charabom Shardra!"). Shown on Charabom Select in Mesen.

effect: Own Ox Battra, the legendary Charabom (Lv 40)
note: GameShark, cart RAM: $A1E8, Charabom 27. Shown on Charabom Select in Mesen.

effect: Own any Charabom, including the other version's ten
note: GameShark, cart RAM: the 30-entry roster $A110 + 8 x id ([owned, id, level, three stats, 0, 0]) is the same in all five versions; only the stages that hand them out differ. All 30 owned at once in Mesen (all five versions): every card shows. 80vv12A1 + 8 x id sets the level to vv.

Game Genie, compare $CA: $02:52EB JP Z -> JP, so the hit test ($53:4000, via $00:2A0F) never reaches the dying state $3C ($02:5356). Same address and bytes in all five versions. Bot 6,000 frames of 1-01 in each of the five versions: 0 hits (8-9 without). GameShark: the player's flash timer $C752 (+$52, tested at $02:52E0 before the hit test) held at $10; bot 6,000 frames of 1-01: 0 hits in all five versions.

GameShark: lives $C2F7 (decremented at $02:709F after a death; 0 = game over) held at 3. Bot 6,000 frames in each version: 11-13 deaths, lives stay 3, no game over. Game Genie: DEC A -> AND A at $02:709F (Ain $02:70D0); bot 6,000 frames: 11-13 deaths, lives stay 3 (all five).

effect: A new game flags all 95 stages of both versions, against 75 in each retail version
note: The new-game template copied to cart RAM $A030 (a word per stage, 19 per world, read by $53:4D0E) has every stage's flag set in the Ain Version. Each retail version clears the flag of the 20 stages only the other version has (55 are shared); Blue matches Hikari and Red matches Yami. Read from cart RAM after a new game in Mesen in all five versions; not played through to those stages.

code: ↑ ↓ Select Start ↓ ↑ Start Select ↑ ↓, then A
effect: Charabom Battle against a computer rival instead of over the infrared link
note: On the Charabom Battle OK? screen (Selected highlighted); Battle Game needs a saved file. The sequence checker $08:4B28 (table $08:4B77, the same in all five versions) sets $C4E3 = 1 after ten right presses; a wrong press sets it to $FF until the screen is opened again. A then goes to scene $15 instead of the NETWORK screen and loads a rival from $08:4C24 (indexed by a frame counter). Typed in Mesen on all five versions through to Round 1 Start! (Japan: 1かいせんめ かいし!), e.g. Draco against アクアドラゴン Lv 38 on Hikari.

effect: The certificate: the Japanese versions add a red seal by the signature and a rating picture; the US ones print the rating as text
note: Hikari and Yami draw sprite group $0B at X $7C, Y $70 ($02:712B, called from $02:7122), Ain the same at $02:715C; in Blue and Red $02:712B is a bare RET. JP loads one of 7 rating graphics to VRAM $88C0 ($02:713E); US picks a text rating from $C198 in steps of 10. A random-input bot reached real game overs on Blue and Hikari in Mesen; Red and Yami have the same bytes. Image: Blue, Hikari.

effect: A Pentel HI-POLYMER Ain logo after the Hudson logo
note: $00:0258-$026A sets $C198 = 1, draws the logo screen ($00:04D8, loader $01:4000 picks tiles $01:4B01 and map $01:5301), waits $28 frames, then draws the Hudson logo with $C198 = 0. Hikari makes one call (the Hudson logo). Seen in Mesen at boot with no input.

code: Put the cart in an original Game Boy
effect: The US versions go straight to the "Game Boy Color only" screen; the Japanese ones show the Hudson logo first (Ain also the Pentel logo)
note: Hikari and Yami call the logo ($00:050F) at $00:029B-$02C5 before the lockout; Blue and Red lack those 18 bytes; Ain shows both logos ($00:02B8-$02DD). Seen in Mesen with the model set to Game Boy. Image: Blue's lockout, the Hudson logo of Hikari and Ain, Ain's Pentel logo.

effect: An unused starfield picture: galaxies, sparkles and the edge of a planet
note: Max loads 2 KB graphics blocks from the table at $1A:705A (254 entries, the same in all five versions). Of all the 2 KB slots in the graphics banks, $46:4000 is the only one no entry points to (entries 199 and 200 both point at $46:4800), and no code reads bank $46 directly; the data is the same in all five. Shown in Mesen (Blue) by pointing entry $43 (file $6B123, loaded by the title) at it and writing tiles 0-127 into the title's BG map, in the title's palette (its own palette is unknown).

effect: A hiss nothing plays, and a rising phrase only the sound test plays
note: Every sound goes through one routine ($00:181D in Blue; $C1A0 = function, $C1A1 = number), from 376 calls with the number written in and three tables; none gives 0D or 1A. 1A is on the sound test's list ($52:5D0F), 0D on no list. 0D is a noise hiss of about 1.6 s that dies away; 1A a square-wave phrase of about 1.7 s that gets louder. The effect data is the same in all five. Recorded in BizHawk (Blue).
